mechanism: Isoniazid induces CYP3A4, reducing darunavir plasma concentrations and potentially compromising antiretroviral efficacy; darunavir may inhibit isoniazid metabolism via CYP2C9/CYP2C19.
action: Monitor darunavir efficacy closely; consider therapeutic drug monitoring for darunavir levels; ensure adequate tuberculosis treatment response and watch for hepatotoxicity from both agents.
